age.evidence: All mice used were C57Bl6/J and at least 12 weeks of age, but no more than 5 months, at the time of surgery.

sex.evidence: female mice performed fewer trials on DOI compared to saline (Figure 1D; Wilcoxon signed rank test, p = 0.011, n = 12), whereas male mice did not show a significant difference (Figure 1D; Wilcoxon signed rank test, p = 0.39, n = 10).

dosing.evidence: Drugs were administered IP 5 min prior to behavioral testing. (±)-DOI hydrochloride (DOI) (Sigma-Aldrich, #D101) was dissolved in sterile physiological saline and injected at a fixed volume of 5 mL/kg at a dose of 3 mg/kg.

handling.evidence: No handling protocol is described in the methods.

group_housing.evidence: Animals were group housed on a reverse 12:12 h light cycle.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were group housed on a reverse 12:12 h light cycle. All behavioral testing was performed during the dark cycle.

assays.assay_description: Two-alternative choice odor navigation task in a custom arena. Mice poke an initiation port, then navigate toward the side (left/right) emitting a turbulent 2-PE odor plume and poke the reward port for water; 10% odor-omission trials; variable ITI 1–15 s; fixed 40-min sessions. DOI (3 mg/kg i.p.) or saline given 5 min before testing in a within-subject crossover (≥1 week apart). Measures: accuracy (overall and in 5-min bins), trials completed, ITI repokes, false reports, reward port duration, trial and ITI duration, DLC-derived speed, sniff frequency via nasal thermistor, arena occupancy, and HTR rate/location scored from video during the same session.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered IP 5 min prior to behavioral testing.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were trained until they performed at 85% accuracy for 1 week, which varied per mouse but took less than 2 weeks total.

setup_restrain.evidence: this work advances our understanding of how the psychedelic DOI alters olfactory search behavior and sniff in freely moving mice.

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were given ad libitum unless otherwise specified for water restriction; no food is described in the testing arena (only water rewards).

water_restriction.evidence: Mice were water restricted and maintained at a minimum of 80% baseline weight for training and experiments.

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were then administered 3 mg/kg DOI or saline then placed into the task 5 min later.

sample_size.evidence: Wilcoxon signed rank test, p = 0.024, n = 22 ... n = 12 [female] ... n = 10 [male]; 'The number of mice used in repoke and false report analyses was 17'; sniff signal n = 14 (DOI), 13 (saline).

outcomes.summary: Acute 3 mg/kg DOI decreased olfactory search accuracy, reduced trials completed (driven by females), increased reward port duration and odor-trial duration, decreased movement speed, and increased sniff frequency. ITI repokes, ITI duration and false reports were unaffected; HTRs occurred preferentially closer to the odor-port end of the arena with no trial vs ITI or sex difference.
outcomes.statistics: Accuracy: Wilcoxon signed rank, p = 0.024, n = 22. Trials completed: p = 0.011, n = 22 (females p = 0.011, n = 12; males p = 0.39, n = 10). ITI repokes: p = 0.27, n = 17. Reward port duration (correct): rank sum p < 0.001, n = 17; median signed rank p = 0.002. Incorrect trials: DOI odor vs DOI omission p < 0.001, vs saline odor p = 0.030, vs saline omission p < 0.001; median p = 0.21 (omission p = 0.049). Odor trial duration p < 0.001; ITI duration p = 0.19. Speed within trial p = 0.011; ITI p = 0.036. Sniff frequency: Fisher-Pitman Z = 24.9, p < 0.001; odor Z = 3.38, p < 0.001; omission Z = 2.71, p = 0.007; ITI Z = 18.4, p < 0.001; median sniff p = 0.11. HTR location: X-coordinate permutation p = 0.002 (trial), p < 0.001 (combined); Y p = 0.92; trial vs ITI p = 1; sex p = 0.31.
outcomes.evidence: Mice more often navigated to the incorrect side of the arena in the DOI condition (Figure 1B; Wilcoxon signed rank test, p = 0.024, n = 22). ... Mice completed fewer trials in the DOI condition (Figure 1D; Wilcoxon signed rank test, p = 0.011, n = 22). This effect was driven by female mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Accuracy, trials completed, ITI repokes, false reports, reward port duration, trial duration, ITI duration, speed, sniff frequency, occupancy, HTR rate/location.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: To ask how DOI impacted performance as a function of time in the session, we quantified accuracy in 5 min time bins.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: KP-MoSeq syllables were obtained but no transition, sequence or bout-structure results are reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Sniffing (active investigative sampling) directly measured: 'sniff frequency was higher in DOI sessions'.

B5_social.evidence: Olfactory search task with no social component; mice tested individually.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Mice were trained until they performed at 85% accuracy for 1 week (learned odor-guided operant task).

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The location of the nose, head, left and right ears, body, left and right hips, and tail base were tracked via DeepLabCut ... Tracked videos were analyzed in Keypoint Motion Sequencing (KPMoSeq) to obtain behavioral syllables.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only separate univariate tests (Wilcoxon, permutation, KS) reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Custom operant-style behavioral arena with initiation and reward ports.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge described in the arena.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in the arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Only task ports described; no enrichment objects.

E6_spatial.evidence: Arena divided only by a virtual 'decision line' and quadrants used for real-time scoring ('A correct response was registered when the mouse entered the corresponding quadrant'); no physical walls/dividers described.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice tested individually in the arena.

E8_food_water.evidence: To receive a water reward, mice had to navigate toward higher odor concentration (water delivered in reward ports during session).

D1_continuity.evidence: mice were assigned to start in the DOI or saline condition then crossed over into the other condition at least 1 week later.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Sessions were at a fixed duration of 40 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Two test sessions per mouse (DOI and saline), at least 1 week apart.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline data reported; saline crossover session serves as control.

D5_followup.evidence: Testing began 5 min after injection; no recording ≥24 h post-dose reported.

D6_circadian.evidence: Sessions were at a fixed duration of 40 min.

judge_notes: All candidates identified a single Olfactory Search Task assay; HTR, sniffing (thermistor), occupancy and speed were all measured within the same 40-min task session and kept within this one assay entry.
B7 set to 1 (2/3 candidates): DeepLabCut pose estimation and KP-MoSeq syllables are explicitly on the rubric's score-1 list.
B1 value corrected to '7+' (gemma4 had score 3 with value '4-6').
E6 overridden to 0 against all candidates: the arena's zones (decision line, quadrants) are virtual; the paper describes no physical walls/dividers, and the rubric scores virtual zones as 0.
E8 set to 1 (modal): water delivered via reward ports during recording.
food_restriction set to 'during' per rubric default (no food in arena; ad lib food in home cage); water_restriction 'before' (water-restricted to 80% weight).
time_dependent set to n/a since drug–test interval was a single timepoint (within-session binning noted under B2).
